figures.finding: Brunei has no rule of its own for child performers: no one may employ a child (under fifteen) save, from fourteen, in light work suited to his capacity outside industry (a doctor's certificate decides); a person under sixteen cannot enter a contract of service, and from sixteen to eighteen only in an occupation the Commissioner of Labour approves. The exception for an industrial undertaking employing only the child's family (s. 103(2)), which the file held until 2026-11-03 from the 2009 text, was deleted by the Employment (Amendment) Order, 2015.

value.from16to18: occupation approved by the Commissioner of Labour

figures.applies: Brunei, Employment Order 2009 ss. 2, 9, 103 (as amended by S 50/2015), the Attorney General's Chambers' English text.

sources.said: "child" means a person who has not attained the age of 15 years
No person shall employ a child in an industrial undertaking or in an undertaking which is not an industrial undertaking, except as provided for in subsections (2) and (3).
A child who has attained the age of 14 years may be employed in light work suited to his capacity in an undertaking which is not in industrial undertaking.
For the purposes of subsection (3), a certificate of a medical practitioner shall be conclusive on the question of whether any work is suited to the capacity of any particular child.

A person who has not attained the age of 16 years shall not be capable of entering into a contract of service. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other written law, a person who has attained the age of 16 years but who has not attained the age of 18 years shall be capable of entering into a contract of service in an occupation approved by the Commissioner

sources.title: Employment Order, 2009 (S 37/2009), English text, Attorney General's Chambers, Brunei Darussalam (found by its WordPress search, wp-json/wp/v2/media?search=employment+order), ss. 2, 9, 103
sources.said: "child" means a person who has not attained the age of 15 years; ... A person who has not attained the age of 16 years shall not be capable of entering into a contract of service. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other written law, a person who has attained the age of 16 years but who has not attained the age of 18 years shall be capable of entering into a contract of service in an occupation approved by the Commissioner as not being injurious to the moral and physical development of youths. ... No person shall employ a child in an industrial undertaking or in an undertaking which is not an industrial undertaking, except as provided for in subsections (2) and (3). ... (3) A child who has attained the age of 14 years may be employed in light work suited to his capacity in an undertaking which is not in industrial undertaking. (4) For the purposes of subsection (3), a certificate of a medical practitioner shall be conclusive on the question of whether any work is suited to the capacity of any particular child.
